# The Cloud That Glows in the Dark

## Scripture

**"Then Moses said, 'Now show me your glory.' And the Lord said, 'I will cause all my goodness to pass in front of you, and I will proclaim my name, the Lord, in your presence.'"** — Exodus 33:18–19

## Reflection

Binoculars reveal what the naked eye misses. Point them toward the constellation Orion, and the middle "star" of his sword resolves into something breathtaking—the Orion Nebula, a vast cloud of gas and dust glowing softly in the dark, where new stars are being born.

The Orion Nebula shouldn't shine at all. It produces no light of its own. Its brilliance comes entirely from stars within it, pouring their radiance onto the surrounding dust. Without those stars, the cloud would be invisible—cold, dark, unnoticed.

Moses understood this. Standing on Sinai, he knew he had nothing luminous in himself to offer. So he asked for the one thing that would make him shine: "Show me your glory." And God, in breathtaking mercy, agreed—letting His goodness pass by, letting His own radiance fall upon a humble man.

This is the promise hidden in the nebula. We are dust—beloved dust, but dust nonetheless. We generate no light. Yet the Light of the World has chosen to dwell within us, and His radiance makes us glow with a brightness that is entirely His.

In this fall season, when the nights grow long and Orion climbs high, let the glowing cloud remind you: you were never meant to shine on your own. You were meant to be illuminated.

## Prayer

Lord, I have no light of my own. Like that distant cloud, I am dark until You shine upon me. Show me Your glory, and let Your goodness pass before me today. Make my life a reflection of Your radiance, that others might see Your brightness in my ordinary dust. Amen.
